reasoning_traces.think:
The Brier decomposition splits forecast performance into three orthogonal terms: reliability (deviation from perfect calibration), resolution (ability to distinguish between classes), and uncertainty (inherent variability of outcomes). This allows GSI to isolate sources of forecast inefficiency. Isotonic calibration ensures that predicted probabilities are monotonically increasing with true likelihood, preventing overconfidence artifacts. Reliability curves provide empirical validation by aggregating forecasts into bins and comparing mean predicted vs actual outcomes. These primitives form a closed-loop system where calibration improves prediction quality, which in turn enhances situational awareness in GSE.
